cards.title: Blazin' Hot Chicken
cards.subtitle: Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Use the published late schedule as a planning check: it lists service until 2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A chicken-focused counter-service stop with especially late listed hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge lists Blazin' Hot Chicken as open until 2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late Night Bites in Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 10 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday; 10 a.m.–3:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday. Confirm holiday changes before leaving.

cards.title: Coffee Call
cards.subtitle: Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Plan a Friday, Saturday, or Sunday evening visit when the published late-hours listing says beignets and café au lait are available until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A beignet-and-coffee option with midnight service on select nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge states that Coffee Call serves until 12 a.m. on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays.

cards.title: KOK Wings & Things
cards.subtitle: Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Make this a weekend food pickup: the published schedule lists midnight closing Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A wings-and-fries stop whose listed hours extend into the early morning on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge lists KOK Wings & Things until 12 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late Night Bites in Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 11 a.m.–12 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11 a.m.–2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; confirm before travel.

cards.title: Midnight Munchies
cards.subtitle: Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Use the Tuesday–Saturday window for a late meal; the published listing says this food stop stays open through 1 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A late-week food destination with a listed 1 a.m. closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge lists Midnight Munchies as open from 8 p.m. to 1 a.m. Tuesday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late Night Bites in Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Listed late hours: 8 p.m.–1 a.m. Tuesday–Saturday. Check for schedule changes before making the trip.

cards.title: The Original Raising Cane's – Highland
cards.subtitle: Highland Road, Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Use the Highland location’s published late schedule for an after-evening food run, with later hours Thursday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: The original Highland Road location has listed service into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge lists The Original Raising Cane's – Highland until 2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late Night Bites in Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 9 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 9 a.m.–3:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; verify holiday hours.

cards.title: Schlittz And Giggles – Downtown
cards.subtitle: Third Street, Downtown Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Plan this downtown pizza pickup for Friday or Saturday, when the published listing gives a 3 a.m. closing time.
cards.short_summary: A downtown pizza destination with listed 3 a.m. weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge lists the downtown Schlittz And Giggles location as open until 3 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.source_title: Late Night Bites in Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Listed late hours are until 3 a.m. Friday and Saturday at the downtown location; check same-day availability.

cards.title: Smalls Sliders – Nicholson
cards.subtitle: Nicholson Drive, Baton Rouge
cards.notes: For a campus-side late food run, use the published Thursday–Saturday schedule, which lists this Nicholson location through 3 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Nicholson Drive slider stand with listed 3 a.m. hours on select nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge lists Smalls Sliders – Nicholson until 12 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late Night Bites in Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 10:30 a.m.–12 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 10:30 a.m.–3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; verify before going.

cards.title: Whataburger #1205
cards.subtitle: 5851 Creek Centre Drive, Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Use this Creek Centre Drive location when a fully overnight dining room is useful; its official location page lists 24-hour dine-in and drive-thru service.
cards.short_summary: A Baton Rouge Whataburger officially listed as open around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Whataburger’s official location page lists both dine-in and drive-thru service as 24 hours every day at 5851 Creek Centre Drive.
cards.source_title: Whataburger #1205 — Creek Centre Drive
cards.access_notes: Official listing: dine-in and drive-thru are 24 hours daily; curbside hours differ and holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Waffle House #442
cards.subtitle: 2363 College Drive, Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Use the College Drive location for a sit-down food stop at any hour; its official location page lists 24-hour service Monday through Sunday.
cards.short_summary: A College Drive Waffle House officially listed as open 24 hours daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House’s official page lists Waffle House #442 at 2363 College Drive as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Waffle House #442 — College Drive
cards.access_notes: Official listing: 24 hours Monday–Sunday. Check the location page for temporary operational updates.

cards.title: Waffle House #2380
cards.subtitle: 855 South Staring Lane, Baton Rouge
cards.notes: Keep this south-of-campus option in mind when you need a food destination outside conventional evening hours; the official locator lists it as open 24 hours.
cards.short_summary: A Staring Lane Waffle House with official 24-hour status.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House’s official Baton Rouge locator lists Waffle House #2380 at 855 South Staring Lane as open 24 hours.
cards.source_title: Waffle House locations in Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Official locator shows this location as open 24 hours; check the store listing before departing for exceptional closures.

boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named LSU spaces for studying, group work, reading, walking, and taking a break between classes, based on current university sources.

cards.title: Spread Out in the Quad
cards.subtitle: Outdoor focus and people-watching at LSU’s academic core
cards.notes: Bring notes or a laptop when the weather cooperates; use the open Quad for solo review while staying amid the rhythm of campus.
cards.short_summary: An open-air study option that keeps you connected to campus movement.
cards.evidence_claim: An April 2026 LSU feature identifies the Quad as a place where students focus, learn, and occasionally people-watch during finals.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; weather and university event restrictions may affect use.

cards.title: Settle Into Hill Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Quiet study amid Special Collections
cards.notes: Choose Hill when you need fewer distractions and a quieter atmosphere; confirm current library hours and designated quiet periods first.
cards.short_summary: A calm library setting with distinctive natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature says Hill Memorial Library offers designated quiet hours, a peaceful study environment, and notable lighting.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Library access and quiet-hour rules vary; check LSU Libraries before visiting.

cards.title: Regroup on the Union’s First Floor
cards.subtitle: Flexible seating for work and between-class breaks
cards.notes: Use the mixed seating for a quick work session or informal meetup, keeping busier periods in mind if your task requires concentration.
cards.short_summary: A central, flexible landing place for studying or meeting classmates.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 feature documents first-floor Student Union seating and describes the Union as supporting group work, breaks, and studying.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to LSU Student Union operating hours, events, and building policies.

cards.title: Find the Third-Floor Study Pods
cards.subtitle: Divided workstations with charging access
cards.notes: Head upstairs when you want more separation than the main floor; bring your charger and leave the shared pods ready for the next student.
cards.short_summary: A quieter Union option designed around focused laptop work.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 feature says the Student Union’s third floor has quieter study pods with built-in dividers and charging stations.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Shared pods are available only while the Student Union is open and may be occupied.

cards.title: Take Group Work to the Terrace
cards.subtitle: Fresh-air tables beside the Student Union
cards.notes: Move a project meeting outside for sunlight and room to talk; check the forecast and relocate indoors during heat, rain, or campus events.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor extension of the Union for solo work or small-group projects.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 feature identifies the Student Union Terrace as a place to sit alone or meet a group and work on projects outdoors.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating is weather-dependent and may be affected by Student Union events.

cards.title: Study Beneath the Memorial Oaks
cards.subtitle: Shaded tables with a World War I memorial context
cards.notes: Pause at a table beneath the oaks for reading or review, and treat the grove respectfully as a memorial to LSU students lost in World War I.
cards.short_summary: A shaded study stop whose trees carry individual commemorative meaning.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 feature says students sit at tables and study in Memorial Oak Grove, where each tree honors an LSU student lost in World War I.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial space near the Student Union; use may be affected by weather or events.

cards.title: Use the BEC Rotunda Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Indoor seating inside the Business Education Complex
cards.notes: Choose a seat in the Rotunda for coursework between nearby classes, while respecting any building access rules and scheduled academic activity.
cards.short_summary: A spacious indoor study setting within LSU’s business complex.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature identifies the Business Education Complex Rotunda as offering numerous places for students to study.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Access follows Business Education Complex building hours and university rules.

cards.title: Reset in the BEC Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Benches and greenery just outside the business complex
cards.notes: Take reading or a short review session to a courtyard bench; use it as a brief outdoor reset when spring plantings and weather allow.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped bench setting for slowing down between academic tasks.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 feature documents benches, greenery, and seasonal blooms in the Business Education Complex Courtyard as a place to sit and study.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Outdoor courtyard use is weather-dependent and subject to adjacent building policies.

cards.title: Read or Walk Through the Enchanted Forest
cards.subtitle: A shady path behind the Student Health Center
cards.notes: Use the shaded path for a short walk or bring a book for a quiet pause; stay on established campus areas and respect other visitors.
cards.short_summary: A tree-covered campus retreat suited to reading and restorative walks.
cards.evidence_claim: An LSU Student Affairs profile identifies the Enchanted Forest behind the Student Health Center as a shady walking spot where students hang hammocks and read.
cards.source_title: Amy Ordeneaux | LSU Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus area behind the Student Health Center; visit in daylight and account for weather.

cards.title: Meet in the French House Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Honors collaboration space across from the Sternberg Salon
cards.notes: Honors students can use the first-floor lounge for study groups and campus activities; confirm eligibility and building access before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated Honors space for collaborative work inside a historic building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ogden Honors College states that the first-floor French House Student Lounge is designed for Honors students to gather for study groups and campus activities.
cards.source_title: Our Campus | Ogden Honors College
cards.access_notes: Intended for Ogden Honors students; access depends on French House hours and college policies.

boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified LSU-area activities requiring neither admission nor a purchase, including campus museums, gardens, art, wildlife viewing, and transit.

cards.title: See Mike at His Campus Habitat
cards.subtitle: Wildlife viewing on North Stadium Drive
cards.notes: Check Mike’s official social accounts before meeting friends there, since maintenance or animal-care needs may keep him inside.
cards.short_summary: Watch LSU’s live tiger from the public viewing area beside the stadium district.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that the Tiger Habitat is on North Stadium Drive and that there is no fee to see Mike the Tiger.
cards.source_title: Visit Mike the Tiger
cards.access_notes: No fee. Mike is usually outside daily between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m., but times vary; Thursday-morning yard work can delay access.

cards.title: Explore Nine Natural-History Dioramas
cards.subtitle: Free exhibits inside Foster Hall
cards.notes: Meet inside Foster Hall for a self-guided look at the dioramas and interactive displays; contact the museum before bringing a large group.
cards.short_summary: Compare Louisiana wildlife and other natural-history specimens in a compact campus exhibit.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum says its Foster Hall exhibit area, containing nine dioramas and interactive exhibits, is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Museum of Natural Science
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; large groups should follow the museum’s group-visit instructions.

cards.entity_name: William A. Brookshire LSU Military Museum
cards.title: Trace LSU’s “Ole War Skule” History
cards.subtitle: A free history stop in Memorial Tower
cards.notes: Plan a weekday visit with a friend and use the exhibits to connect LSU’s military origins with the university’s later history.
cards.short_summary: Explore artifacts and stories documenting LSU’s military heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies the William A. Brookshire LSU Military Museum as free and open to the public Monday through Friday.
cards.source_title: Honoring the Past While Committing to the Future
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–3 p.m.

cards.title: Wander Hilltop’s Native-Plant Landscape
cards.subtitle: Fourteen acres of paths, meadow, pond, and woodland
cards.notes: Go during daylight, cross the footbridge, and pause by the meadow or bamboo grove; follow posted rules protecting plants and animals.
cards.short_summary: Take an unhurried walk through a free public arboretum devoted to Southern native plants.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU says Hilltop Arboretum’s grounds are open to the public free of charge seven days a week during daylight hours.
cards.source_title: Hilltop Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Grounds are free and open daily from dawn to dusk. Public restrooms are available Tuesday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

cards.entity_name: Children's Garden at LSU AgCenter Botanic Gardens
cards.title: Look for Butterflies and Edible Plants
cards.subtitle: A no-fee garden walk at Burden
cards.notes: Start in the butterfly garden, read the host-plant labels, then compare the seasonal fruit and vegetable plantings toward the rear.
cards.short_summary: Turn a garden stroll into a group scavenger hunt for caterpillars, butterflies, fruit, and vegetables.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that the Children’s Garden is open to the general public seven days a week and that there is no fee to visit.
cards.source_title: Children's Garden | LSU AgCenter Botanic Gardens
cards.access_notes: No fee; open to the general public Monday–Sunday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Teachers planning field trips should register in advance.

cards.entity_name: Trees and Trails at LSU AgCenter Botanic Gardens
cards.title: Walk Three Miles of Burden Woods Trails
cards.subtitle: Woodland paths at the Botanic Gardens
cards.notes: Check in at the Welcome Center, choose a comfortable woodland loop, and keep the paid Windrush Gardens outside this zero-dollar outing.
cards.short_summary: Share a shaded hike through the woods, wetlands, and arboretum portions of Burden.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU describes Trees and Trails as three miles of walking paths, while its visitor handbook states Botanic Gardens admission is free except for Windrush Gardens.
cards.source_title: Burden Museum & Gardens Volunteer Handbook
cards.access_notes: Botanic Gardens admission is free except for Windrush Gardens. Current site instructions require all visitors to check in.

cards.entity_name: Alfred C. Glassell Jr. Exhibition Gallery
cards.title: See Contemporary Art at Glassell Gallery
cards.subtitle: Free LSU School of Art exhibitions downtown
cards.notes: Choose a Thursday for the extended public hours, then meet inside the gallery to compare reactions to the current exhibition.
cards.short_summary: View rotating contemporary work presented by LSU’s School of Art without paying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s College of Art & Design states that admission to Glassell Gallery and its programs is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: College of Art & Design | Glassell Gallery
cards.access_notes: Free and open to all. The cited LSU page lists Tuesday–Sunday noon–5 p.m., with extended hours to 7 p.m. Thursday and Friday; confirm before travel.

cards.title: Browse LSU Museum of Art for Free
cards.subtitle: Student-ID admission at the Shaw Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Bring a valid student ID for free entry, ride downtown with friends, and check the museum site first for current exhibitions and closures.
cards.short_summary: Spend an afternoon with regional and national art on the fifth floor of the Shaw Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s current admission page states that students with ID enter free; it also offers free admission to everyone on each month’s first Sunday.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission — LSU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Students receive free admission with valid ID. Everyone receives free admission on the first Sunday of each month during museum hours.

cards.title: Take a Free Tiger Trails Loop
cards.subtitle: Campus and nearby neighborhoods by transit
cards.notes: Pick an operating fixed route, meet at an established stop, and ride a loop together; verify the live schedule around holidays and breaks.
cards.short_summary: See more of campus and nearby Baton Rouge from LSU’s fare-free bus network.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Parking and Transportation says Tiger Trails provides free bus service for students, faculty, staff, and visitors on and off campus.
cards.source_title: FAQs | LSU Parking and Transportation
cards.access_notes: No fare for students, employees, or visitors. Fixed routes generally follow weekday schedules and may be reduced or suspended during breaks and holidays.

cards.entity_name: LSU Museum of Art Free First Sunday
cards.title: Make Art Together on Free First Sunday
cards.subtitle: Monthly no-admission museum day downtown
cards.notes: Schedule the group for the first Sunday, confirm that month’s program online, and use the free-access window without adding a purchase.
cards.short_summary: Pair gallery viewing with the museum’s recurring public free-admission day.
cards.evidence_claim: The LSU Museum of Art states that admission is free for everyone on the first Sunday of every month.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission — LSU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Free to the public on the first Sunday of every month; the museum lists Sunday hours of 1–5 p.m. Confirm the calendar before visiting.

boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented LSU settings for solo work, group sessions, presentation practice, and outdoor reading, with current access constraints noted.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Collaborative Study Rooms
cards.title: Bring the Group to a Screen-Ready Room
cards.subtitle: Bookable rooms for collaborative work in LSU’s Main Library
cards.notes: Reserve ahead for a two-to-six-person session, then bring a laptop for the room display’s supplied HDMI or USB-C connection.
cards.short_summary: A reservable group workspace with a display, whiteboard, and seating for small teams.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries says these Main Library rooms accommodate groups of two to six; its room guidance identifies displays, whiteboards, and supplied display cables.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | LSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available to LSU undergraduate and graduate students. Study spaces close one hour before the library; reservations take priority over walk-up use.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Student Meeting Rooms
cards.title: Practice the Presentation Behind a Door
cards.subtitle: Enclosed Main Library rooms built around a large display and table
cards.notes: Use the enclosed setup to rehearse slides aloud; reserve no more than three hours for the day and return borrowed peripherals afterward.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed option for presentation rehearsal or a focused project meeting.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries describes the Student Meeting Rooms as enclosed rooms with a large display and table, suitable for presentation practice and reservable for up to three hours per day.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | LSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available to LSU undergraduate and graduate students. An individual student may reserve one for up to three hours per day; spaces close one hour before the library.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Quiet Study Rooms
cards.title: Keep the Group Session Quiet
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms for two to six quiet collaborators
cards.notes: Choose this room when the team needs shared space without a loud discussion, and keep the session within the three-hour daily limit.
cards.short_summary: Small-group rooms where collaboration comes with an explicit quiet-use expectation.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries says its Quiet Study Rooms accommodate quiet groups of two to six in the Main Library and may be reserved for up to three hours per day.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | LSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available to LSU undergraduate and graduate students. Reservations are limited to three hours per individual student per day; spaces close one hour before the library.

cards.entity_name: LSU Main Library Bookable Study Booths
cards.title: Settle Into a Booth With Power
cards.subtitle: Individual Main Library booths with a desk, lamp, and outlet
cards.notes: Reserve a booth for sustained individual work, use a temporary-storage locker if needed, and never leave books or belongings unattended.
cards.short_summary: A bookable individual station equipped for laptop work and close reading.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries states that every bookable study booth has a desk, reading lamp, and electrical outlet and can be reserved by undergraduate and graduate students.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | LSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: LSU undergraduate and graduate students may reserve a booth daily for up to 14 consecutive days. Ask the Checkout Desk about a lock for temporary storage.

cards.title: Take the Reading Outside in the Quad
cards.subtitle: A central outdoor LSU setting for books, notes, and a laptop
cards.notes: Bring material that works outdoors and pick a comfortable place in the Quad; have an indoor backup ready if weather disrupts the session.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable central-campus alternative to an indoor desk or study room.
cards.evidence_claim: An April 2026 LSU photo feature identifies The Quad as a place where students focus and learn during finals.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: The official feature documents outdoor studying here but does not state hours, reservation rules, or building-style access controls.

cards.entity_name: Hill Memorial Library Quiet Study Room
cards.title: Work Quietly on Hill’s Second Floor
cards.subtitle: A weekday quiet-study room inside Hill Memorial Library
cards.notes: Plan this stop for a weekday between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., finish food or drinks in the lobby, and keep the study room quiet.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room with defined weekday access and a no-food-or-drink rule.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Libraries says Hill Memorial Library’s second-floor Quiet Study Room is open to students on semester weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; food and drink are prohibited there.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | LSU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open to students during the semester on weekdays, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Food and drink are prohibited in the room but may be consumed in the first-floor lobby.

cards.entity_name: LSU Student Union Third-Floor Study Pods
cards.title: Plug In at a Divided Study Pod
cards.subtitle: Third-floor Union pods with charging stations and built-in dividers
cards.notes: Head to the Union’s third floor when you need a divided workstation, and bring the charging cable required for your own device.
cards.short_summary: A more separated Union workstation with built-in charging support.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature documents third-floor Student Union study pods with built-in dividers and charging stations.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Located on the Student Union’s third floor. The cited feature does not provide operating hours or state whether individual pods can be reserved.

cards.title: Move the Project to the Terrace
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Union seating for solo work or a group project
cards.notes: Use the terrace for work that benefits from fresh air, secure loose papers before opening them, and shift indoors if conditions change.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor study setting suited to either independent work or meeting a project group.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature says the Student Union Terrace lets students sit outside alone or meet with a group to work on projects.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: Outdoor terrace access may depend on Student Union operations and conditions; the cited source gives no hours or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Find a Work Surface in the BEC Rotunda
cards.subtitle: An indoor Business Education Complex setting with multiple study places
cards.notes: Use the Rotunda for an indoor session between campus commitments, and confirm building access before planning evening or weekend work.
cards.short_summary: A spacious academic-building interior documented by LSU as a place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature identifies the Business Education Complex Rotunda as offering numerous places for students to study.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: The source documents study use but does not specify public access, room reservations, or current building hours; verify access before going.

cards.title: Study Among the BEC Courtyard Greenery
cards.subtitle: An outdoor Business Education Complex space with benches
cards.notes: Pack a compact study task for a courtyard bench, check the weather first, and keep an indoor alternative ready for heat or rain.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped outdoor option for reading or completing a shorter assignment.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s April 2026 study-spaces feature documents benches and greenery in the Business Education Complex Courtyard as a setting where students can sit and study.
cards.source_title: Photos: Study Spaces that Carry LSU Students through Finals
cards.access_notes: The cited source confirms outdoor study seating but does not state hours, reservations, or whether building closures restrict courtyard access.

boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, map-listed stops on the Northgate, Highland Road, Chimes Street, Lake Street, and Nicholson Drive corridors beside LSU.

cards.title: The Chimes — Highland Road
cards.subtitle: Highland Road corridor, LSU Northgate
cards.notes: Use the Highland Road location for its made-from-scratch menu; check the restaurant’s current menu and service details before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Northgate restaurant with a documented made-from-scratch menu.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chimes lists its Highland location at 3357 Highland Road and describes a made-from-scratch menu.
cards.source_title: The Chimes
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service; confirm current hours and seating directly with the venue.

cards.title: Highland Coffees — Highland Road
cards.subtitle: Highland Road corridor at Chimes Street
cards.notes: Order a coffee or tea, then use the shop’s courtyard or seating for a reading break; the business places itself by LSU’s historic North Gates.
cards.short_summary: Coffee and tea shop at LSU’s historic North Gates.
cards.evidence_claim: Highland Coffees says it has operated since 1989 near the Highland Road–Chimes Street corner at LSU’s historic North Gates.
cards.source_title: About Highland Coffees
cards.access_notes: Commercial coffee shop; purchases are optional for viewing the location, but menu items require payment.

cards.title: Varsity Theatre — Highland Road
cards.subtitle: Highland Road corridor, LSU Northgate
cards.notes: Check the event calendar and ticket rules before planning a show; the historic venue is a clearly photographed landmark along the Northgate strip.
cards.short_summary: Historic event venue on the Northgate stretch of Highland Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Baton Rouge identifies Varsity Theatre at 3353 Highland Road near LSU and describes it as a historic event venue.
cards.source_title: Varsity Theatre | Visit Baton Rouge
cards.access_notes: Event access varies by program; review the specific event’s age and ticket requirements.

cards.title: Roul’s Deli — Highland Road
cards.subtitle: Highland Road corridor, LSU Northgate
cards.notes: Use this stop for sandwiches, burgers, salads, or hot plates; the listed Highland location is a short Northgate-side option beside campus.
cards.short_summary: Deli-format meal stop on Highland Road near LSU.

boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented LSU rituals, honors, songs, objects, and game-day practices drawn from current university and athletics sources.

cards.title: Meet the Living Face of LSU
cards.subtitle: LSU’s live-tiger mascot tradition
cards.notes: Visit Mike’s campus habitat respectfully, follow posted guidance, and use LSU’s history page to identify each tiger in the lineage.
cards.short_summary: A student-funded idea became an enduring live-mascot program represented today by Mike VII.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that Mike VII arrived on campus on August 15, 2017, and continues a live-mascot program established more than 85 years ago.
cards.source_title: About LSU: What Is LSU Known For? And Other LSU Facts
cards.access_notes: Observe Mike only from public visitor areas and follow all habitat rules; animal appearances are not guaranteed.

cards.title: Line the Route on Victory Hill
cards.subtitle: The team-and-band procession before LSU home football games
cards.notes: Check the official game-day schedule, then stand along the designated public route early enough to watch the team and Tiger Band pass.
cards.short_summary: Players, musicians, and generations of spectators converge on one ceremonial approach to Tiger Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU reports that before every home game, fans line the street while the Golden Band from Tigerland parades the football team down Victory Hill and plays the Pregame Salute.
cards.source_title: Saturday Night in Death Valley: An LSU Game Day Through Students’ Eyes
cards.access_notes: This occurs on LSU home-football game days; consult the current official event schedule and observe route controls.

cards.title: Answer the First Four Notes
cards.subtitle: Tiger Band’s ceremonial Tiger Stadium entrance
cards.notes: Be in position before kickoff and listen for the opening four notes; join the crowd’s LSU response without blocking aisles or entrances.
cards.short_summary: Four notes from the Golden Band cue a stadium-wide response before the Tigers take the field.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU describes its pregame show as a tradition in which the opening four notes of the Pregame Salute prompt the crowd to chant “LSU” as the band lines up.
cards.source_title: Saturday Night in Death Valley: An LSU Game Day Through Students’ Eyes
cards.access_notes: Presented inside Tiger Stadium before football games; stadium entry requires the applicable event credential.

cards.title: Stay for the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: The student section’s ritual after a Tiger Stadium win
cards.notes: After a home victory, remain through the band’s alma mater and follow the student section’s lead while stadium departure begins around you.
cards.short_summary: A win closes with students swaying together as the band plays LSU’s alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU documents that after every Tiger Stadium victory, the student section sways and sings while the band plays the LSU Alma Mater.
cards.source_title: Saturday Night in Death Valley: An LSU Game Day Through Students’ Eyes
cards.access_notes: This contingent postgame ritual occurs inside Tiger Stadium after LSU victories; event admission is required.

cards.title: Clap Along Before Kickoff
cards.subtitle: Tiger Stadium’s recorded pregame singalong
cards.notes: Listen just before kickoff for the opening notes, then clap or sing from your seat while keeping stairs and stadium circulation paths clear.
cards.short_summary: A Garth Brooks recording turns the minutes before kickoff into a coordinated LSU crowd ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics states that every home game, immediately before kickoff in Tiger Stadium, “Callin’ Baton Rouge” plays and fans stand, clap, and sing along.
cards.source_title: Gameday Soundtrack
cards.access_notes: Occurs inside Tiger Stadium at LSU home football games; event admission is required.

cards.title: Spell Out Tigers After the Score
cards.subtitle: The band-and-crowd response to an LSU touchdown
cards.notes: After an LSU touchdown, listen for Tiger Band’s motif and join the spelled-out response from your seat without entering restricted areas.
cards.short_summary: A short band cue converts each LSU touchdown into a collective spelling lesson.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics documents that after a Tigers touchdown, the band plays the “Tiger Rag” motif and fans respond by spelling out “T-I-G-E-R-S.”
cards.source_title: Gameday Soundtrack
cards.access_notes: This score-triggered ritual occurs inside Tiger Stadium during football games; event admission is required.

cards.title: Look for White on the Home Side
cards.subtitle: LSU football’s inverted home-uniform convention
cards.notes: At a home game, photograph the team’s white jerseys from your assigned area and compare the combination with LSU’s documented uniform history.
cards.short_summary: LSU’s home team often wears the color normally associated with visiting football teams.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics traces its home-white-jersey tradition to the 1958 national-championship season and says the practice returned in 1995 after a rules change.
cards.source_title: Football to Wear Traditional White Jerseys in BCS Game
cards.access_notes: Uniform combinations vary by game; verify the current matchup through LSU Athletics before relying on this tradition.

cards.title: Spot the Double-Post Silhouette
cards.subtitle: A preserved LSU football-field tradition
cards.notes: From an authorized stadium seat or broadcast view, compare the double-support goalpost shape with the conventional single-post design.
cards.short_summary: Tiger Stadium preserves an old-fashioned goalpost profile as a deliberate piece of LSU football identity.
cards.evidence_claim: An official LSU Athletics letter identifies the H-style goalposts among LSU football’s time-honored traditions.
cards.source_title: A Letter From Joe Alleva - July 2016
cards.access_notes: View from authorized stadium areas during an event or tour; never enter the playing field without permission.

cards.title: Let Mike Watch Over the Rings
cards.subtitle: The LSU Ring’s pre-ceremony overnight ritual
cards.notes: Order by the published deadline if eligible, then follow Student Affairs instructions so your ring can join the overnight habitat tradition.
cards.short_summary: Eligible LSU rings spend a ceremonial night under Mike’s watch before their owners receive them.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Student Affairs states that rings ordered by its stated deadline may participate in Overnight with Mike, when Mike watches over the rings in his habitat overnight.
cards.source_title: LSU Ring
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited by LSU Ring eligibility, purchase, ordering deadlines, and current ceremony instructions.

cards.title: Recognize Twelve Graduating Tigers
cards.subtitle: LSU’s annual senior honor built around scholarship, leadership, and service
cards.notes: Read the current eligibility rules, nominate an eligible senior by the posted deadline, or follow LSU’s announcement of the new class.
cards.short_summary: Each spring, LSU distills a graduating class into twelve examples of campus and community contribution.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Student Affairs states that each spring it recognizes 12 outstanding seniors who contribute positively to campus, the surrounding community, or society.
cards.source_title: Tiger Twelve
cards.access_notes: Applications and nominations are limited to published eligibility windows; viewing the recipient page is public.

boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: Your First Weekend at Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College, Shared as Ca
boards.description: An under-21-safe Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning LSU’s central landmarks, recreation options, gathering spaces, and ways to find future campus activities.

cards.title: Start at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Friday evening orientation stop
cards.notes: Locate the information desk, scan the building directory, and identify a comfortable meeting point before exploring farther.
cards.short_summary: Learn the practical center of campus before the weekend gets underway.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies a second-floor information desk for questions about the Student Union and campus; normal Friday building hours extend to 10 p.m. during fall and spring semesters.
cards.source_title: Auxiliary Services
cards.access_notes: Normal fall and spring hours are Friday 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; reduced interim, holiday, closure, and event schedules may apply.

cards.title: Build a Weekend Shortlist
cards.subtitle: Friday event-planning check
cards.notes: Create your TigerLink profile, filter the current listings by interest, and save one future organization or campus event.
cards.short_summary: Turn a quiet first evening into a plan for meeting people later.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU describes TigerLink as its platform for discovering student organizations and events, registering for activities, and tracking involvement.
cards.source_title: Using TigerLink | LSU Campus Life
cards.access_notes: TigerLink is an online platform; individual events may require registration, LSU credentials, or separate eligibility checks.

cards.title: Cross the Historic Quad
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning campus bearings
cards.notes: Walk the main paths, note the surrounding academic buildings, and choose an easy landmark for future meetups.
cards.short_summary: Use LSU’s historic core to establish a mental map of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies the Quadrangle as the historic core of campus, completed before the 1926 dedication and used as a main walking thoroughfare.
cards.source_title: The Quad at LSU: The Heart of Campus, both Lush and Inviting
cards.access_notes: Remain on established pedestrian routes and observe temporary restrictions or university notices affecting outdoor areas.

cards.title: Read the Mounds’ Story
cards.subtitle: Saturday respectful history stop
cards.notes: Study the interpretive panels from outside the protected area, then leave the fragile earthworks completely undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: Encounter the site’s Indigenous history while following its preservation rules.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU says the Campus Mounds are publicly accessible historic earthworks, but visitors must admire them from a safe distance and may not walk, sit, or slide on them.
cards.source_title: LSU Campus Mounds | A Native American Mounds Historical Site
cards.access_notes: View from a safe distance, obey posted rules and protective barriers, and never climb, sit, slide, or bicycle on the mounds.

cards.title: Pause for the Alma Mater Chimes
cards.subtitle: Saturday noon landmark stop
cards.notes: Reach the tower plaza before noon, view the World War I memorial exterior, and listen for the scheduled alma mater chime.
cards.short_summary: Connect a recognizable campus landmark with its memorial purpose.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that Memorial Tower honors Louisianans who died during World War I and that the tower chimes the LSU Alma Mater at noon.
cards.source_title: Visit Campus | LSU
cards.access_notes: The noon chime is documented by LSU; this stop is framed around the exterior plaza, not assumed museum entry.

cards.title: Visit Mike’s Habitat
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon mascot stop
cards.notes: Read the tiger-conservation displays, observe quietly from the public viewing area, and accept that Mike may be indoors.
cards.short_summary: Meet LSU’s live mascot through a welfare-conscious public visit.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU locates the Tiger Habitat on North Stadium Drive, states there is no fee to visit, and says Mike is usually outside daily between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m., with times varying.
cards.source_title: Visit Mike the Tiger
cards.access_notes: Mike is usually outside 8 a.m.–7 p.m., including weekends, but availability varies for animal care, maintenance, and yard work.

cards.title: Reserve a Tiger Stadium Tour
cards.subtitle: Saturday book-ahead campus landmark
cards.notes: Check the official calendar first, buy a timed ticket at least a day ahead, and arrive at the Bill Lawton Room as directed.
cards.short_summary: See the stadium interior through an authorized guided visit.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics offers approximately 45-minute guided Tiger Stadium tours on select dates, with advance ticket purchase required at least 24 hours before the scheduled start.
cards.source_title: LSU Athletics Guided Tours
cards.access_notes: Tours operate only on listed dates, require tickets at least 24 hours ahead, and begin at the Bill Lawton Room; the route may change.

cards.title: Try the Climbing Area
cards.subtitle: Saturday active campus stop
cards.notes: Check the live schedule and eligibility, wear closed-toe shoes, then ask staff about orientation before attempting a route.
cards.short_summary: Sample campus recreation while learning the facility’s safety process.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU UREC documents a climbing area with top-rope and bouldering walls and requires participants to check in, follow equipment rules, and pass testing before belaying.
cards.source_title: Climbing Area | LSU University Recreation
cards.access_notes: Verify current open-climb hours and entry eligibility; check in at the desk, wear closed-toe shoes, and follow all posted climbing policies.

cards.title: Loop Part of University Lake
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning outdoor reset
cards.notes: Choose a manageable out-and-back walk, stay aware of cyclists and uneven edges, and turn back before heat or fatigue builds.
cards.short_summary: Begin Sunday with an adaptable lakeside walk close to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Campus Life explicitly recommends walking, running, riding, or skating the University Lakes as an LSU activity.
cards.source_title: 101 Things to Do at LSU | LSU Campus Life
cards.access_notes: Use established public routes, account for weather and ongoing restoration conditions, and follow all posted detours or safety notices.

cards.title: Finish on the Parade Ground
cards.subtitle: Sunday route-recap stop
cards.notes: Face the surrounding landmarks, retrace the weekend route on your phone, and save two dependable meeting points for later.
cards.short_summary: Close the weekend by connecting its stops into one usable campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies the Parade Ground as a named central campus green used for university gatherings, including the recurring Fall Fest tradition.
cards.source_title: Fall Fest | LSU Campus Life
cards.access_notes: The open lawn may be reserved or restricted for scheduled events; observe posted notices and avoid organized sports or cleats.

warnings: Tiger Stadium tours require advance purchase and are offered only on select dates.
UREC access, eligibility, reservations, and activity hours should be checked immediately before visiting.
Outdoor stops may be affected by weather, university events, construction, or game-day controls.
